Annual Crop Land: Annual Crop Land appears as cultivated fields with rectangular, strip-like, or circular parcels. Rows, alternating tones, bare soil, and seasonal vegetation create organized agricultural patterns, with field boundaries and access tracks often visible. Surrounding land cover provides additional boundary and scale cues.
Forest: Forest appears as dense continuous tree cover with coarse granular texture and dark to medium green tones. Individual crowns are usually indistinct, while irregular natural boundaries and uniform canopy density separate it from cropland and open vegetation. Large-scale shape and local texture provide the strongest recognition cues.
Herbaceous Vegetation Land: Herbaceous Vegetation Land appears as open ground covered by low vegetation, producing smooth to lightly mottled green or yellow-green textures. Large continuous patches lack the dense crown pattern of forest and usually show fewer regular boundaries than cultivated fields. Spatial continuity and neighboring regions help define the class visually.
Highway or Road: Highway or Road appears as long narrow linear structures with smooth gray or pale surfaces. Roads may curve, intersect, and connect built areas, while their continuous geometry and relatively uniform width distinguish them from rivers, paths, and field boundaries. Surrounding land cover provides additional boundary and scale cues.
Industrial Buildings: Industrial Buildings appears as clusters of large rectangular roofs, broad paved areas, and regularly arranged structures. Roofs are often gray, white, or blue, with straight edges, large footprints, loading areas, and road connections forming a geometric built-up pattern. Large-scale shape and local texture provide the strongest recognition cues.
Pasture Land: Pasture Land appears as broad grassy parcels with mostly smooth green textures and irregular or softly bounded field shapes. Color is often more uniform than annual cropland, with few dense structures and occasional tracks, hedges, or small patches dividing open vegetation.
Permanent Crop Land: Permanent Crop Land appears as agricultural parcels containing repeated rows or regularly spaced vegetation. Linear or dotted planting patterns, orchard-like spacing, and stable field organization distinguish it from smoother pasture and seasonally bare annual crop fields. Surrounding land cover provides additional boundary and scale cues.
Residential Buildings: Residential Buildings appears as dense mixtures of small roofs, streets, yards, and compact blocks. Repeated small rectangular structures, varied roof colors, narrow road networks, and limited open space create a finer-grained built texture than large industrial complexes. Large-scale shape and local texture provide the strongest recognition cues.
River: River appears as an elongated winding water body with dark blue, green, or brown tones. Width varies along its course, banks form irregular parallel boundaries, and branching or meandering geometry distinguishes it from straight roads and broad lakes. Spatial continuity and neighboring regions help define the class visually.
Sea or Lake: Sea or Lake appears as a large continuous water region with smooth, uniform blue, dark, or greenish tones. Shorelines form broad irregular boundaries, while the absence of dense internal texture and the large contiguous area distinguish it from narrow river channels.
